stimuli.text: A block of mass 5 kg on a 30° incline is connected by a light string over a light, frictionless pulley at the top of the incline to a hanging block of mass 5 kg. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the incline is 0.1. The system is released from rest, and the hanging block descends.
A block of mass 1.9 kg on a horizontal frictionless surface is attached to a spring. Its position is $$x(t) = 0.15\cos(11t)$$, with x in meters and t in seconds.
Students measure the period of a simple pendulum for several string lengths, using small amplitudes.
A solid cylinder (I = ½MR²) and a hoop (I = MR²) of equal mass M and radius R are released from rest at the top of the same ramp of height 2.7 m. Both roll without slipping.

questions.stem: A particle's position is $$x(t) = -3t^3 + 3t^2 + 0t$$, with x in meters and t in seconds. What is its velocity at $$t = 2$$ s?

options.why: Bring each exponent down as a factor when differentiating.
Recheck the arithmetic.
That is the position; differentiate it.
Correct. Differentiate once: v = 3at² + 2bt + c.

questions.explanation: v(t) = -9t² + 6t + 0, so at t = 2 the value is -24.

questions.stem: A curve of radius 50 m is banked so that a car at 17 m/s needs no friction. What is the banking angle?

options.why: Correct. tan θ = v²/(rg).
Measure the angle from the horizontal.
Use tan θ = v²/(rg), from dividing the force components.
Square the speed.

questions.stem: A system obeys $$\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} = -49x$$. What is the period of its motion?

options.why: ω is the square root of the coefficient.
T = 2π/ω.
T = 2π/ω, not 2πω.
Correct. ω = √49 = 7 rad/s, T = 2π/ω.

questions.stem: Two springs with constants 30 N/m and 30 N/m are connected in parallel and support a 4 kg mass at rest. How far do they stretch in total?

options.why: Both springs share the load.
Correct. k_eq = k₁ + k₂.
Series and parallel rules are reversed.
The force is the weight, mg.

questions.stem: Masses of 4 kg and 3 kg hang on either side of a light, frictionless pulley. What is the tension in the string?

options.why: The lighter mass accelerates up, so T exceeds its weight.
Use T = m₂(g + a).
The heavier mass accelerates down, so T is less than its weight.
Correct. T = 2m₁m₂g/(m₁ + m₂).

questions.stem: A planet has 3 times Earth's mass and 3 times Earth's radius. What is the gravitational field strength at its surface? (Earth's is 9.8 N/kg.)

options.why: The ratio is inverted.
g decreases with radius.
Correct. g ∝ M/R².
g depends on 1/R², not 1/R.

questions.stem: A force $$F(x) = 2x^3$$ N acts along the x-axis. How much work does it do on an object moving from $$x = 2$$ m to $$x = 4$$ m?

options.why: The force is not constant.
Divide by n + 1 when integrating.
Correct. W = ∫F dx.
Integrate; do not just evaluate F.

questions.stem: A boat points straight across a river 170 m wide, moving at 5 m/s relative to the water. The current flows at 2 m/s. How far downstream does the boat land?

options.why: Use the crossing time w/v_boat.
Correct. The current does not change the time to cross; it only carries the boat downstream.
That is a time, not a distance.
Drift = current speed × crossing time.

questions.stem: A wheel spinning at 28 rad/s slows uniformly to rest in 19 s. How many revolutions does it make while stopping?

options.why: That is in radians; convert to revolutions.
The average angular speed is ω₀/2.
Correct. Δθ = ½ω₀t, then divide by 2π.
Recheck the average.

questions.stem: A uniform rod of length 2 m swings about a pivot at one end with small amplitude. What is its period?

options.why: I = mL²/3.
A rod is a physical pendulum, not a simple one.
Correct. T = 2π√(I/(mgd)) with I = mL²/3 and d = L/2.
d is L/2, the distance to the center of mass.

questions.stem: A 1 kg ball hits a wall at 13 m/s and rebounds at 9 m/s. The contact lasts 0.05 s. What is the average force from the wall?

options.why: Correct. Δp = m(v_f − v_i) with the direction reversed.
Include the rebound.
Divide by time.
The velocity reverses, so the speeds add.

questions.stem: An oscillator's position is $$x(t) = 0.07\cos(11t)$$ m. What is its maximum acceleration?

options.why: That is v_max.
Multiply by the amplitude.
Correct. a_max = Aω².
Differentiate twice: Aω².

questions.stem: A constant torque of 3 N·m acts on a wheel ($$I = 0.3$$ kg·m²) initially at rest, through 4 revolutions. What is the wheel's final angular speed?

options.why: Correct. Work τΔθ (in radians) equals ½Iω².
Convert revolutions to radians.
W = ½Iω².
½Iω² = W; solve for ω.

questions.stem: A motor lifts a 370 kg load 5 m at constant speed in 9 s. What average power does it deliver?

options.why: Correct. P = mgh/t.
P = W/t.
Include g.
That is the work; divide by time.

questions.stem: A 88 kg person stands on a scale in an elevator that is accelerating downward at 1 m/s². What does the scale read?

options.why: Include gravity.
The acceleration changes the normal force.
Correct. The scale reads the normal force: N − mg = ma (up positive).
Check the direction of the acceleration.

questions.stem: A ball rolls off a horizontal ledge 18.5 m high at 6 m/s. How far from the base of the ledge does it land?

options.why: Correct. Fall time from the height, times the horizontal speed.
Fall time is √(2h/g).
Take the square root for the time.
Horizontal and vertical motion are independent.

questions.stem: A uniform rod of length 0.5 m is pivoted at one end and released from rest in a horizontal position. What is its angular acceleration just after release?

options.why: Use τ = Iα with I = ML²/3.
The weight acts at L/2.
Correct. τ = Mg(L/2) and I = ML²/3 give α = 3g/(2L).
τ = MgL/2.

questions.stem: A 1000 kg car heading east at 5 m/s collides with a 3000 kg car heading north at 17 m/s, and they lock together. What is their speed just after the collision?

options.why: Momentum is a vector; add components at right angles.
Correct. Conserve momentum in x and y separately, then combine.
Weight each velocity by its mass.
Divide by the total mass.

questions.stem: A 2.5 kg ball on a 1.2 m string moves in a vertical circle. At the top of the circle its speed is 6 m/s. What is the tension in the string there?

options.why: Centripetal force uses v².
Check the direction of gravity relative to the center.
Include gravity.
Correct. At the top, T + mg = mv²/r.

questions.stem: Satellite B orbits a planet in a circular orbit 4 times the radius of satellite A's circular orbit. What is the ratio of B's orbital speed to A's?

options.why: Correct. v = √(GM/r), so v ∝ r^(−1/2).
Farther satellites move more slowly.

questions.stem: A 1 kg ball moving at +3 m/s collides elastically head-on with a 2 kg ball at rest. What is the velocity of the 2 kg ball afterward (positive in the original direction)?

options.why: That would be a sticking collision.
Only equal masses exchange velocities.
Kinetic energy is conserved too.
Correct. Elastic: conserve momentum and kinetic energy (relative velocity reverses).

questions.explanation: v₁' = (m₁ − m₂)v/(m₁ + m₂) = -1 m/s; v₂' = 2m₁v/(m₁ + m₂) = 2 m/s.

questions.stem: A block starts from rest and slides 3 m down a 37° incline with coefficient of kinetic friction 0.3. What is its speed at the bottom?

options.why: Friction removes energy.
Use the vertical drop, L sin θ.
Friction depends on the normal force, mg cos θ.
Correct. mgh − μmg cos θ·L = ½mv².

questions.stem: A planet has mass $$9 \times 10^{23}$$ kg and radius $$2 \times 10^{7}$$ m. What is the escape speed from its surface? ($$G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}$$ N·m²/kg²)

options.why: Potential energy uses 1/R.
Take the square root.
That is the circular orbit speed; escape needs √2 times more.
Correct. ½mv² = GMm/R.

questions.stem: A ball is launched from level ground at 20 m/s at 20° above the horizontal. Ignoring air resistance, what is its time of flight?

options.why: Correct. Treat horizontal and vertical motion separately.
Use v₀ sin θ.
That is the time to the top; the flight is twice as long.
Use the vertical component.

questions.explanation: v₀x = 18.8 m/s, v₀y = 6.84 m/s. T = 2v₀y/g = 1.4 s.

questions.stem: A block slides down a 40° incline. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.3. What is the magnitude of its acceleration?

options.why: Friction depends on the normal force, mg cos θ.
Friction acts up the slope.
The component along the incline is mg sin θ.
Correct. a = g(sin θ − μk cos θ).

questions.stem: A uniform disk of mass 6 kg and radius 0.6 m rotates about an axis perpendicular to it, 0.5 m from its center. What is its rotational inertia?

options.why: The axis is not through the center.
The parallel-axis term is Md².
Correct. Parallel-axis theorem: I = ½MR² + Md².
Include the disk's own I about its center.

questions.stem: A spring with $$k = 110$$ N/m is compressed 0.1 m and launches a 1 kg block across a frictionless surface. What is the block's speed after leaving the spring?

options.why: Take the square root.
Use energy: v = x√(k/m).
The ½ appears on both sides.
Correct. ½kx² = ½mv².

questions.stem: A 2 kg cart moving at 12 m/s collides with and sticks to a 1 kg cart at rest. What is their speed after the collision?

options.why: The carts share the momentum.
Correct. Momentum is conserved; kinetic energy is not.
Kinetic energy is not conserved here.
Use m₁v₁ for the initial momentum.

questions.explanation: v_f = 2·12/3 = 8 m/s; kinetic energy lost = 48 J.

questions.stem: A solid cylinder rolls without slipping from rest down a ramp of height 3.8 m. What is its speed at the bottom?

options.why: Some energy goes into rotation.
Correct. mgh = ½mv²(1 + β) with I = ½MR².
Rotational energy is ½Iω² = ½βmv².
That is only correct for a hoop.

questions.stem: The potential energy of a particle is $$U(x) = 4x^3 - 21x$$ J. At what positive x is the particle in stable equilibrium?

options.why: Set the derivative, not U, to zero.
dU/dx = 3ax² − b.
Correct. Equilibrium where dU/dx = 0; stable at a minimum.
Take the square root.

questions.explanation: dU/dx = 12x² − 21 = 0 gives x = 1.32 m; d²U/dx² > 0 there, so it is stable.

questions.stem: A 15 g bullet moving at 200 m/s embeds in a 1.3 kg block hanging from strings. How high does the block rise?

options.why: h = V²/(2g).
Kinetic energy is not conserved in the collision.
Find the block's speed after the collision first.
Correct. Momentum for the collision, then energy for the swing.

questions.explanation: V = 2.28 m/s after the collision; h = V²/(2g) = 0.266 m.

questions.stem: A 6 kg object at rest experiences a net force $$F(t) = 10t$$ N from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 3$$ s. What is its final speed?

options.why: Correct. Impulse ∫F dt equals the change in momentum.
The force is not constant.
Divide by the mass to get speed.
Integrate the force over time.

questions.explanation: J = ∫F dt = 45 N·s; v = J/m = 7.5 m/s.

questions.stem: A rod lies along the x-axis from $$x = 0$$ to $$x = 5$$ m and has linear mass density $$\lambda = kx^3$$. Where is its center of mass?

options.why: The rod is not uniform.
Integrate x·xⁿ and xⁿ correctly.
Correct. x_cm = ∫xλ dx / ∫λ dx.
The exponents are n + 2 and n + 1.

questions.stem: A uniform 5 m beam weighing 500 N rests on supports at both ends. A 200 N load sits 1 m from the left end. What force does the right support exert?

options.why: Correct. Take torques about the left support.
That is the left support's force.
The load is not at the center.
Include the beam's weight at its center.

questions.stem: A block starts from rest and slides 3 m down a 30° incline with coefficient of kinetic friction 0.1. What is its speed at the bottom?

options.why: Correct. mgh − μmg cos θ·L = ½mv².
Friction depends on the normal force, mg cos θ.
Use the vertical drop, L sin θ.
Friction removes energy.

questions.stem: A thin spherical shell rolls without slipping from rest down a ramp of height 3.1 m. What is its speed at the bottom?

options.why: That is only correct for a hoop.
Some energy goes into rotation.
Rotational energy is ½Iω² = ½βmv².
Correct. mgh = ½mv²(1 + β) with I = ⅔MR².

questions.stem: A mass on a spring oscillates with angular frequency 12 rad/s and amplitude 0.2 m. What is its speed when it is 0.02 m from equilibrium?

options.why: Speed is greatest at equilibrium, not at the ends.
That is the maximum speed, at x = 0.
Correct. v = ω√(A² − x²), from conservation of energy.
Use A² − x² under a square root.

questions.stem: An object of mass 1.8 kg falls from rest with a drag force $$F = -bv$$, where $$b = 0.11$$ kg/s. What is its terminal speed?

options.why: Solve mg = bv for v.
Drag here is linear in v.
Correct. At terminal speed, mg = bv.
That is the time constant.

questions.explanation: v_T = mg/b = 160 m/s and τ = m/b = 16.4 s.

questions.stem: A 1 kg mass hangs from a light string wrapped around a uniform disk pulley of mass 1 kg that turns on a frictionless axle. What is the acceleration of the mass?

options.why: Correct. a = mg/(m + M/2), using I = ½MR² and a = Rα.
I/R² = M/2.
For a disk, I/R² = M/2.
The pulley's inertia reduces the acceleration.

questions.explanation: mg − T = ma and TR = ½MR²(a/R) give a = 6.53 m/s².

questions.stem: An object's acceleration is $$a(t) = 5t$$ m/s². At $$t = 0$$ it has velocity 3 m/s and is at $$x = 0$$. What is its velocity at $$t = 4$$ s?

options.why: Correct. Integrate a(t) and add the initial velocity.
The acceleration is not constant, so constant-acceleration equations do not apply.
Include the initial velocity.
Integrating tⁿ divides by n + 1.

questions.title: Block on an incline with a hanging mass

parts.prompt: Draw (describe) a free-body diagram for the 5 kg block, labeling each force.

rubric.criterion: Weight down, normal force perpendicular to the incline, tension up the incline.
Kinetic friction down the incline (opposite the motion).

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the acceleration of the system in terms of the masses, θ, μ and g, then calculate its value.

rubric.criterion: Newton's second law applied to each block (or the system).

parts.prompt: Calculate the tension in the string.
Calculate the speed of the blocks after the hanging block has descended 1 m, and the work done by friction on the incline block during that motion.

rubric.criterion: Work by friction, with a negative sign.

parts.prompt: Sketch (describe) graphs of position, velocity and acceleration versus time for one period, aligned vertically.

rubric.criterion: Position is a cosine starting at +A; velocity is a negative sine starting at 0.
rubric.example: x starts at 0.15 m; v starts at 0 and goes negative.

rubric.criterion: Acceleration starts at its negative maximum and is opposite in sign to position throughout.

parts.prompt: Derive expressions for v(t) and a(t), and determine the maximum speed and maximum acceleration.
Calculate the spring constant and the period.
Calculate the total mechanical energy and describe how kinetic and potential energy vary during one period.

rubric.example: K is maximum at x = 0 and zero at x = ±A; U is the reverse; the sum is constant. Each varies twice per period.

parts.prompt: Describe a procedure the students could use to measure the period accurately, including how to reduce uncertainty.

rubric.example: Time 10 swings with a stopwatch and divide by 10.

rubric.criterion: Keep the amplitude small and repeat trials.
rubric.example: Release from under about 10° and average several trials.

parts.prompt: Identify quantities to graph that would give a straight line, and explain how g can be found from the graph.
Plot (describe) the linearized data and draw a best-fit line. Use it to calculate an experimental value of g.
The students repeat the experiment with a much larger amplitude. Predict how the measured periods would change and explain.

rubric.criterion: Periods increase slightly; the small-angle approximation (sin θ ≈ θ) no longer holds.
rubric.example: The restoring torque is less than proportional to θ at large angles.

parts.prompt: Without calculating, predict which object reaches the bottom first. Justify your prediction using energy.

rubric.example: It has the smaller rotational inertia per MR².

rubric.criterion: Justification: less of its energy goes into rotation, so more is translational kinetic energy.

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the speed at the bottom of an object with rotational inertia βMR², in terms of g, h and β.

rubric.criterion: Energy conservation including both forms of kinetic energy, with v = Rω.

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of each object at the bottom.
Explain whether your derived expression is consistent with your prediction in part (a), and why neither speed depends on M or R.

rubric.criterion: Smaller β gives larger v, consistent with the prediction.
M and R cancel in the energy equation.
rubric.example: Only the shape factor β matters.
